_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from NadekoBot's own Docker setup (AGPL-3.0).
name: NadekoBot
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: NadekoBot is a Discord bot for moderation, music, games, an economy and more. The egg installs a release with FFmpeg and yt-dlp for its music commands, and it needs a Discord bot token.
startup: export PATH="/home/container/bin:$PATH"; [ -n "$BOT_TOKEN" ] || unset BOT_TOKEN; [ -n "$BOT_OWNERIDS__0" ] || unset BOT_OWNERIDS__0; [ -f data/creds.yml ] || cp data/creds_example.yml data/creds.yml; if [ "{{YT_DLP_AUTO_UPDATE}}" = true ]; then bin/yt-dlp -U 2>&1 | tail -n 1; fi; if [ -z "${BOT_TOKEN:-}" ] && ! grep -qE "^token: *['\"]?[A-Za-z0-9]" data/creds.yml; then if ./NadekoBot --commandlist /tmp/raptor-commands.json >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -s /tmp/raptor-commands.json ]; then echo "NadekoBot works, but needs a Discord bot token: set it in Startup (or in data/creds.yml), then restart the server."; exec sleep infinity; else echo "NadekoBot could not load its commands. Reinstall the server to repair it."; exit 1; fi; fi; exec ./NadekoBot

config.startup: {"done": ["regex:Shard \\d+ ready", "regex:^[^\"]*NadekoBot works, but needs a Discord bot token"]}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# NadekoBot: downloads the chosen release from GitHub (checked against
# GitHub's checksum), with the FFmpeg, yt-dlp and Deno its music commands
# use. Everything in data/ that's already there (creds.yml, the database,
# configs, medusae) is kept; only files the release adds are copied in, and
# the voice libraries in data/lib are always replaced.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
# Downloads unpack in a folder in the server's (the install's /tmp is
# small), removed when the script ends.
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "This server's CPU ($(uname -m)) isn't supported." ;;
esac
download() {
    curl -fsSL -o "$2.part" "$1" || { rm -f "$2.part"; fail "The download failed ($1). Reinstall to try again."; }
    if [ -n "${3:-}" ] && [ "$(sha256sum "$2.part" | cut -d' ' -f1)" != "$3" ]; then
        rm -f "$2.part"; fail "The download didn't match its checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    fi
    mv -f "$2.part" "$2"
}

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
want="${want#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag nadeko-bot/nadekobot "$want") || fail "There's no NadekoBot release $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 7.10.2, then reinstall."
asset="nadeko-linux-$arch.tar.gz"

if [ -x NadekoBot ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-nadeko 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag $arch" ]; then
    echo "NadekoBot $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading NadekoBot $tag"
    gh-release download nadeko-bot/nadekobot "$tag" "$asset" "$work/nadeko.tar.gz" || fail "NadekoBot $tag couldn't be downloaded. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir "$work/new"
    tar -xzf "$work/nadeko.tar.gz" -C "$work/new" --strip-components=1
    rm -f "$work/nadeko.tar.gz"
    [ -x "$work/new/NadekoBot" ] || fail "The NadekoBot $tag download has no NadekoBot program in it."
    # The program: files from the last release that this one dropped go,
    # the rest are replaced. data/ is the bot's own and is handled below.
    if [ -f .raptor-files ]; then
        while IFS= read -r e; do
            if [ -n "$e" ] && [ "$e" != data ] && [ ! -e "$work/new/$e" ]; then rm -rf -- "./$e"; fi
        done < .raptor-files
    fi
    find "$work/new" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name data -printf '%f\n' > "$work/files"
    while IFS= read -r e; do
        rm -rf -- "./$e"
        mv "$work/new/$e" "./$e"
    done < "$work/files"
    mv -f "$work/files" .raptor-files
    # data/: new files only, never the owner's; the voice libraries and the
    # command list always come from the release.
    mkdir -p data/lib
    cp -Rn "$work/new/data/." data/
    cp -f "$work/new/data/lib/"*.so data/lib/
    cp -f "$work/new/data/commandlist.json" data/ 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "$tag $arch" > .raptor-nadeko
fi
mkdir -p data/lib bin
[ -f data/creds.yml ] || cp data/creds_example.yml data/creds.yml

# The arm64 release ships x86 voice libraries: use Debian's Opus and
# libsodium and Discord's own libdave (the same ones NadekoBot's Docker
# image uses) instead.
if [ "$arch" = arm64 ] && [ "$(cat data/lib/.raptor-arm64 2>/dev/null)" != "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Downloading the voice libraries for arm64"
    apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "Debian's package mirror can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    (cd "$work" && apt-get download -qq libopus0 libsodium23 >/dev/null 2>&1) || fail "Opus and libsodium couldn't be downloaded. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir "$work/deb"
    for d in "$work"/*.deb; do dpkg-deb -x "$d" "$work/deb"; done
    cp -fL "$work"/deb/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libopus.so.0 data/lib/opus.so
    cp -fL "$work"/deb/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libsodium.so.23 data/lib/libsodium.so
    gh-release download discord/libdave v1.1.1/cpp libdave-Linux-ARM64-boringssl.zip "$work/libdave.zip" || fail "libdave couldn't be downloaded. Reinstall to try again."
    unzip -qo "$work/libdave.zip" -d "$work/libdave"
    find "$work/libdave" -name libdave.so -exec cp -f {} data/lib/libdave.so \;
    echo "$tag" > data/lib/.raptor-arm64
fi

# FFmpeg: the newest release build for Linux.
ff=https://github.com/FFmpeg-Builds/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/latest
case "$arch" in x64) ffa=linux64 ;; arm64) ffa=linuxarm64 ;; esac
sums=$(curl -fsSL "$ff/checksums.sha256") || fail "FFmpeg's builds can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
line=$(grep -E "  ffmpeg-n[0-9.]+-latest-$ffa-gpl-[0-9.]+\.tar\.xz$" <<<"$sums" | sort -V -k2 | tail -n1)
[ -n "$line" ] || fail "There's no FFmpeg build for this CPU ($arch) right now. Reinstall to try again later."
ffsum="${line%% *}"; ffname="${line##* }"
if [ -x bin/ffmpeg ] && [ "$(cat bin/.ffmpeg 2>/dev/null)" = "$ffsum" ]; then
    echo "FFmpeg is up to date."
else
    echo "Downloading FFmpeg (${ffname%.tar.xz})"
    download "$ff/$ffname" "$work/ffmpeg.tar.xz" "$ffsum"
    mkdir "$work/ffmpeg"
    tar -xJf "$work/ffmpeg.tar.xz" -C "$work/ffmpeg" --strip-components=2 --wildcards '*/bin/ffmpeg' '*/bin/ffprobe'
    mv -f "$work/ffmpeg/ffmpeg" "$work/ffmpeg/ffprobe" bin/
    echo "$ffsum" > bin/.ffmpeg
fi

# yt-dlp: the newest release.
case "$arch" in x64) yta=yt-dlp_linux ;; arm64) yta=yt-dlp_linux_aarch64 ;; esac
yt=https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/latest/download
ytsum=$(curl -fsSL "$yt/SHA2-256SUMS" | awk -v n="$yta" '$2 == n { print $1 }') || true
[ -n "$ytsum" ] || fail "yt-dlp's releases can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
if [ -x bin/yt-dlp ] && [ "$(sha256sum bin/yt-dlp | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$ytsum" ]; then
    echo "yt-dlp is up to date."
else
    echo "Downloading yt-dlp"
    download "$yt/$yta" bin/yt-dlp "$ytsum"
    chmod +x bin/yt-dlp
fi

# Deno: yt-dlp needs a JavaScript runtime to read YouTube.
dtag=$(gh-release tag denoland/deno latest) || fail "Deno's releases can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
case "$arch" in x64) da=deno-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.zip ;; arm64) da=deno-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.zip ;; esac
if [ -x bin/deno ] && [ "$(cat bin/.deno 2>/dev/null)" = "$dtag" ]; then
    echo "Deno is up to date."
else
    echo "Downloading Deno $dtag"
    gh-release download denoland/deno "$dtag" "$da" "$work/deno.zip" || fail "Deno couldn't be downloaded. Reinstall to try again."
    unzip -qo "$work/deno.zip" -d "$work/deno"
    mv -f "$work/deno/deno" bin/deno
    chmod +x bin/deno
    echo "$dtag" > bin/.deno
fi
echo "Installed NadekoBot $tag."

variables.name: Discord bot token
variables.description: The bot's token, from the Discord Developer Portal. Leave it empty to use the one in data/creds.yml.

variables.name: Owner ID
variables.description: Your Discord user ID, which may use the bot's owner commands. More owners go in data/creds.yml.

variables.name: Update yt-dlp at start
variables.description: Update yt-dlp when the bot starts, since YouTube changes often.

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The NadekoBot version to install, such as 7.10.2, or latest. Reinstall to change it.
